body: Power sampling improves large language model (LLM) reasoning at test time by sampling from a sharpened version of the base model's distribution. Its sampler, PowerMH, is slow because its Metropolis--Hastings (MH) updates are sequential: each accept/reject decision sets the state from which the next proposal is generated. Prior work reduces this cost by changing the sampler or the model (e.g., sequential Monte Carlo, approximate lookahead, distillation). We propose Predictive SubTree Prefetching (PreSTO), which accelerates PowerMH by prefetching future proposals and provably leaves its MH transition kernel unchanged. PreSTO views future MH outcomes as a tree of accept/reject decisions: in each model call, it generates the proposals of a prefetched subtree of this tree in one batch, then follows the realized path with the original MH acceptance rule. We also observe that MH reaches only a sparse, nearly unary part of each prefetched subtree, we further design a predictive traversal rule that chooses the subtree to maximize the predicted number of completed transitions. Across seven datasets and five base LLMs, PreSTO achieves median speedups of 1.71×, 1.91×, and 2.33× on PowerMH and its follow-ups EntropyCut and MultiTryMH, respectively; on the first two, it makes a median of 3.9× fewer model calls, each only 2.1× longer. On LCB V6 with Qwen3.5-9B, the predictive traversal rule is a further 1.25×--1.37× faster than the default breadth-first traversal.
summaryZh: 针对大模型推理中Power Sampling采样速度慢的问题，本文提出了预测性子树预取（PreSTO）技术。该方法通过预取未来采样路径并构建决策树，在保持原有Metropolis-Hastings采样内核不变的前提下，实现了显著的推理加速。实验显示，PreSTO在多种数据集和模型上均取得了明显的性能提升，有效降低了模型调用次数。
